investment_summary:
Rubrik's fiscal 2026 showed strong operating momentum: revenue rose 48% to $1.32 billion and Subscription ARR reached $1.46 billion, up 34% [1]. Free cash flow of $237.8 million [1] and a narrower net loss of $348.8 million [1] suggest the model is beginning to fund itself, although deferred revenue growth flattered cash flow and stock-based compensation remains large [1][2].

Valuation is the crux. At the enterprise value of $21.5 billion used in the consensus-dated analysis, the reverse DCF requires about 29% annual revenue growth for ten years, close to the 29.9% three-year historical CAGR and well above the consensus fade to 21.7% in FY2028 [2][3]. On the consensus path the implied return is 5.5% against a 10.3% WACC [3]. The current price therefore assumes sustained hypergrowth. The main risks are channel concentration, with three partners generating about 68% of revenue, and $1.15 billion of convertible notes due 2030 [1]. Consensus and liquidity figures are dated after the 10-K.
key_takeaways: Subscription growth should keep compounding: Subscription ARR rose 34% to $1.46 billion, supporting FY2027 revenue consensus of $1.69 billion [1][3].
Free cash flow should stay positive, but the $237.8 million figure is flattered by a $425.8 million rise in deferred revenue [1][2].
The shares look fully priced: the reverse DCF needs 29% annual growth for a decade, implying a 5.5% return below the 10.3% WACC [2][3].
Channel concentration is the key risk: three partners generated about 68% of fiscal 2026 revenue, so any disruption would hit most sales [1].
business_overview:
Rubrik, Inc. is a Palo Alto-based data security company whose Rubrik Security Cloud (RSC) is a cloud-native SaaS platform that protects data across enterprise, cloud, SaaS, unstructured data and identity providers, combining backup and recovery with cybersecurity on one architecture [1]. For the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026, Subscription ARR reached $1.46 billion, up 34%, and Cloud ARR reached $1.29 billion, up 48%. Average subscription dollar-based net retention stayed above 120%, and customers with at least $100,000 in Subscription ARR rose 25% to 2,805 [1]. Subscription revenue made up about 96% of the $1,316.2 million total [1][2]. The platform is supported by 425 issued U.S. patents and a proprietary data threat engine [1].

The go-to-market model is land-and-expand, run through a direct sales team and a partner network. A vast majority of sales flow through channel partners, and the three largest, Arrow, Exclusive Networks and Ingram Micro, generated about 68% of fiscal 2026 revenue [1]. Appliances built on Super Micro servers still carry much of the hardware footprint, although appliance manufacturing has largely moved to contract manufacturers [1]. Recent initiatives include the July 2025 acquisition of Predibase for $109.1 million to accelerate agentic AI, and Rubrik Agent Cloud (RAC), an AI operations platform commercially available only from February 2026, after the fiscal year closed [1]. Management expects RSC to remain the majority of revenue and the main ARR driver in fiscal 2027 [1].

The capital structure changed materially. In June 2025 the company issued $1.15 billion of 0% convertible notes due 2030 and used the proceeds to repay its $327.9 million credit facility, leaving cash and short-term investments of $1.68 billion [1][2]. Stockholders' equity remains negative at $(519.6) million, reflecting a $3.19 billion accumulated deficit [1]. Analyst consensus as of 2026-11-23 is a Buy rating with a target price of $124.50 (range $110 to $155) [3]. These figures post-date the 10-K and should be read against the share price at that time.
market_position:
Rubrik's end market is enterprise and public-sector data protection and cyber recovery, which the company describes as early-stage and rapidly evolving [1]. Management believes no competitor takes a similar approach, but names Commvault, Dell EMC, IBM, Veeam and Cohesity as main rivals [1]. The filing does not disclose market share, so the position rests on growth and scale comparisons rather than verified share data. International revenue from EMEA and Asia-Pacific rose to $364.5 million from $250.4 million, about 28% of the total, and customers outside the U.S. generated 30% of fiscal 2026 revenue [1].

Customer quality is hard to verify. The filing serves organizations of many sizes across regulated sectors such as banking, healthcare and financial services, plus the public sector, but does not name individual customers, so blue-chip status cannot be confirmed [1]. Concentration sits mainly in channel partners rather than end customers: Arrow, Exclusive Networks and Ingram Micro generated about 68% of revenue in fiscal 2026, down from 73% in fiscal 2025 [1]. Customer behaviour also shows caution, with some customers reducing multi-year upfront payments and contract sizes, and sales cycles lengthening amid cost pressure [1].

Against listed peers, Rubrik looks like a fast-growing challenger rather than an incumbent. In fiscal 2026 it grew revenue 48.5%, against 18.9% for Commvault, 21.9% for SentinelOne and 31.7% for Netskope [4]. Its 80.1% gross margin is close to Commvault's 81.2% and above SentinelOne's 74.1% and Netskope's 68.1% [4]. The classification rests on growth and scale, not on disclosed share, so it should be treated as an estimate [1][4].
operating_results:
Revenue rose 48% to $1,316.2 million in fiscal 2026 from $886.5 million, led by subscription revenue up 53% to $1,263.9 million from $828.7 million, while Other revenue fell 10% to $52.3 million [1][2]. About $70.2 million of subscription revenue came from non-recurring material-rights benefits, so underlying growth is somewhat lower than the headline figure [1]. Cost of revenue dipped 1% to $261.9 million, lifting gross margin to 80% from 70% [1]. Subscription gross margin improved to 82% from 74%, while Other gross margin rose to 39% from 12% on lower stock-based compensation and appliance costs [1].

Operating expenses fell 20% to $1,399.7 million, mainly because stock-based compensation dropped by $584.5 million [1]. That left an operating margin of -26% against -128% a year earlier, and a net loss of $348.8 million against $1,154.8 million, a net margin of -27% from -130% [1]. Loss per share narrowed to $(1.78) from $(7.48), even as weighted shares rose to 196.5 million from 154.3 million [1]. Stock-based compensation of $329.4 million remains large and still drives much of the GAAP loss [1].

Cash generation improved more than earnings. Operating cash flow rose to $282.9 million from $48.2 million, and free cash flow to $237.8 million from $21.6 million [1][2]. The gap to the net loss reflects $329.4 million of stock-based compensation and a $425.8 million rise in deferred revenue from upfront billings, while capital spending was modest at $45.1 million [1]. Consensus normalized EPS for the current year is $0.50, up 60% from $0.31 90 days earlier, and the last four quarters all beat estimates [3]. These forward figures are dated after the 10-K.
risk_assessment:
The most consequential risk is liability from security incidents. Rubrik's core product protects customer data, and the filing warns that a security incident would be especially damaging to its reputation [1]. The Ransomware Recovery Warranty covers eligible customers' recovery costs up to $10 million, and GDPR fines can reach 4% of global annual revenue [1]. The filing also discloses a February 2025 incident in which an unauthorized actor accessed certain log files, and the company says its insurance may not be adequate [1].

Channel and hardware dependence is the second risk. Channel partner agreements are non-exclusive, renew annually and can be terminated at any time without minimum purchase commitments, while the top three partners generated about 68% of revenue [1]. Appliances rely on Super Micro servers, and the filing flags chip shortages and higher server prices as ongoing constraints [1]. Expansion into some countries also depends on recruiting new partners [1].

The third risk combines continued losses, leverage and control. Net losses were $(354.2) million, $(1.15) billion and $(348.8) million across fiscal 2024 to 2026, and the accumulated deficit is $3.19 billion [1]. The $1.15 billion of notes mature in June 2030, and failure to repurchase them upon a fundamental change would constitute a default [1]. Federal net operating losses of $1.97 billion may be limited under Section 382 [1], and Class B holders control about 85% of the voting power [1]. Quality scores add caution: the Altman Z-score of 2.90 sits in the grey zone, and the Piotroski F-score is 5 of 9 [2].

Valuation adds a market risk on top of these operating risks. At the enterprise value of $21.5 billion used in the consensus-dated analysis, the reverse DCF implies a 5.5% return against a 10.3% WACC, so an investor paying today's price needs growth well above a consensus fade [2][3]. Consensus and liquidity figures are dated after the 10-K.
competitors_analysis:
Three peers were chosen from the candidate list, business model first and size second. Commvault (CVLT) is the closest match: it sells data protection and cyber recovery, is named as a competitor in the 10-K, and has 0.8x Rubrik's revenue [1][4]. SentinelOne (S) sells subscription cybersecurity at 0.7x Rubrik's revenue, and Netskope (NTSK) sells SaaS security at 0.5x. Dell and IBM were excluded because their hardware and services models differ too much [4].

Rubrik grew fastest in fiscal 2026, at 48.5%, against 18.9% for Commvault, 21.9% for SentinelOne and 31.7% for Netskope [4]. Its gross margin of 80.1% is close to Commvault's 81.2% [4]. Profitability is weaker: its EBITDA margin of -20.7% trails Commvault's 9.0% but beats SentinelOne's -25.4% and Netskope's -85.6% [4]. Free cash flow of $237.8 million equals an 18% margin, close to Commvault's roughly 20%, while SentinelOne earned about 5% and Netskope about 2% [4]. Return on invested capital is -30.4%, against 8.3% for Commvault [4].

On trailing EV/Sales of 9.18x for fiscal 2026, Rubrik trades above Commvault (2.73x) and SentinelOne (4.56x), and slightly above Netskope (8.8x) [4]. That premium reflects its growth, though Netskope grows more slowly at 31.7%. Consensus forward EV/Sales for FY2027 is 12.7x, with a forward P/E of 211.8x at the current share price [3]. The peer tool and consensus use different price dates, so their multiples should not be combined directly. Commvault shows what profitable, lower-growth software earns in this group, and Rubrik's valuation is supported by growth but not yet by earnings [3][4].

investment_theses.thesis: Subscription growth stays above 25% through fiscal 2027, supporting consensus revenue growth of about 28%.
investment_theses.evidence: Subscription ARR rose 34% to $1.46 billion and Cloud ARR rose 48% [1]. Consensus FY2027 revenue is $1.69 billion, up 28.5%, and the current-year EPS consensus has had 20 upward revisions and no downward revisions in the last 30 days [3].
investment_theses.signpost: Subscription ARR growth at or above 25% in each quarterly report through the Q4 FY2027 report (fiscal year ending January 2027).
investment_theses.invalidation: Subscription ARR growth below 20% in any quarter, or average net retention falling below 120% [1].

investment_theses.thesis: Cash generation is durable, not only a function of upfront billing timing.
investment_theses.evidence: Free cash flow rose to $237.8 million from $21.6 million, but deferred revenue added $425.8 million [1][2]. Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow was $286.2 million at the latest quarter [2].
investment_theses.signpost: Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow at or above the latest $286.2 million [2], with deferred revenue growth slowing, reported with the FY2027 10-K in early 2027.
investment_theses.invalidation: Free cash flow turning negative on a trailing basis, or a decline in deferred revenue [1][2].

investment_theses.thesis: The current valuation requires growth to stay near 29% for a decade; if growth fades to consensus, returns fall below the cost of capital.
investment_theses.evidence: The reverse DCF implies 29.3% annual growth, against consensus of 28.5% for FY2027 and 21.7% for FY2028, and an implied return of 5.5% versus a 10.3% WACC [2][3]. Forward EV/Sales is 12.7x for FY2027 [3].
investment_theses.signpost: FY2027 revenue tracking at or above the $1.69 billion consensus, and FY2028 consensus growth holding above 21.7% in the next consensus update.
investment_theses.invalidation: FY2028 consensus growth cut below 20%, or a shift in analyst revisions from upward to downward over the next 30 days [3].

investment_theses.thesis: Operating leverage narrows losses as gross margin holds near 80% and operating expenses keep falling.
investment_theses.evidence: Gross margin rose to 80% from 70%, and operating margin improved to -26% from -128% [1]. Peer EBITDA margin for Commvault is 9.0% against Rubrik's -20.7% [4]. Consensus normalized EPS for the current year is $0.50, up from $0.31 90 days earlier [3].
investment_theses.signpost: GAAP operating margin improving from -26% in FY2026 toward break-even in the FY2027 results, with gross margin holding at or above the 80% of FY2026 [1].
investment_theses.invalidation: Gross margin falling back toward the 70% of fiscal 2025 [1], or operating margin no better than -26% in the FY2027 results [1].
